name: VARoleDiagnosticianUnexplainedRash

custom.system_prompt: Devon noticed an itchy rash on his arm that wasn't there yesterday and asks Sigma to help him figure out what might have caused it. Sigma asks about recent products, exposures, and the rash's appearance, without diagnosing, and flags when to see a doctor.

initial_prompt: Generate a scene where Devon notices an itchy rash on his arm that wasn't there yesterday and asks Sigma to help him figure out what caused it. Sigma asks about recent new products (soap, detergent, lotion), any new exposures (plants, fabrics, foods), and the rash's appearance and spread, without diagnosing. Sigma flags what would mean he should see a doctor rather than just monitor it. Keep every line short and natural — the opening line already addresses Sigma directly.

user1.name: Devon
user1.tts_prompt: A little anxious, examining his arm

variations.context: Solo evening investigation of a sudden, unexplained itchy rash

setting.mood: Mildly anxious, curious about the cause
setting.relationship_dynamic: Individual working through the problem with Sigma, no one else present
setting.background: Devon can't immediately think of anything that changed, but hasn't thought hard about it yet
setting.conversation_style: Short, slightly anxious sentences that become more specific as he thinks it through

scenario_template.topic: Devon addresses Sigma directly in his first line, folding in the observation — e.g. 'Sigma, I've got this itchy rash on my arm that definitely wasn't there yesterday. Help me figure out what caused it.' One short turn, straight to Sigma.
scenario_template.note: The observation and the ask arrive together.

scenario_template.topic: Sigma asks whether he's used any new soap, detergent, or lotion recently, and whether he's been anywhere with new plants or fabrics — narrowing toward a contact-irritant cause.
scenario_template.note: Devon's answer should reveal something concrete — e.g. he switched laundry detergent a few days ago.

scenario_template.topic: Given the new detergent, Sigma asks about the rash's shape and location relative to where clothing sits against skin, and whether it's spreading or staying contained, to support or weaken the contact-irritant hypothesis.
scenario_template.note: This checks whether the pattern actually matches contact dermatitis rather than something else.

scenario_template.topic: Sigma explains that the pattern is consistent with a reaction to the new detergent, suggests switching back and monitoring, and names symptoms that would mean he should see a doctor instead — spreading rapidly, swelling, difficulty breathing.
scenario_template.note: Sigma is clear this is a plausible explanation, not a certain diagnosis.

scenario_template.topic: Devon reacts, relieved to have a plausible explanation and plan, but still keeping an eye on it. Keep this realistic.

user1.name: Devon
user1.role: Enthusiastic aspiring filmmaker, mildly anxious about a sudden unexplained rash. Speaks in short, slightly anxious sentences that get more specific as he thinks it through. Ends relieved by a plausible explanation but still watchful.

assistant.name: Sigma
assistant.role: Diagnostician. Structures a skin-symptom investigation by asking about recent product changes, exposures, and the rash's specific pattern, without diagnosing. Names concrete symptoms that would warrant seeing a doctor.

conversation_structure: The opening line already addresses Sigma directly, folding in the observation
Sigma structures the investigation (recent changes, exposures, pattern) rather than jumping to a verdict
Sigma names concrete escalation criteria (rapid spread, swelling, breathing difficulty)
Every line is one or two short spoken sentences
The resolution is a plausible explanation and monitoring plan, not a certain diagnosis
assistant_behavior: Sigma does not diagnose a specific skin condition
Sigma checks whether the pattern actually matches the leading hypothesis before proposing it
